title: prefill handoff CLI and quant-adoption fallback
author: Sofia Patel
description:
Motivation: customers running mixed workloads reported oscillations when tenant defaults for batching/caching and quantization were applied simultaneously. This PR introduces a small ops-friendly CLI (prefill-handoff) plus a runtime component that scores tenant readiness for enabling compact quant profiles and applies a safe fallback plan if unit-econ or latency regressions are observed. The goal is to automate adoption of cost-saving defaults while minimizing blast radius and giving operators deterministic dry-run and rollback tools.

What changed (high level):
- CLI: new command `redwood prefill-handoff` with subcommands `scan`, `dry-run`, `apply`, and `rollback`. The CLI emits a deterministic plan and optionally writes a JSON preview to S3.
- Adopter service: pkg/econ/adopter implements a lightweight adoption score based on recent latency/throughput trends, token-unit-econ delta, and coldstart sensitivity. Scores are tenant-scoped and computed from existing telemetry without additional instrumentation.
- Fallback plans: runtime/prefill/handshake adds the ability to register a fallback chain (e.g., reduce batch target, disable compact quant on a model family, enable prefix caching) which is executed automatically when configurable thresholds are breached.
- Telemetry: new metrics econ.adoption_score, econ.plan_preview_size, econ.fallback_triggered with tags (tenant_id, model_family, profile). These plug into existing dashboards and alert rules.
- Tests & safety: end-to-end simulator in benchmark-lab added a `prefill-handoff` scenario that runs historical traces and asserts <=1.5% quality regression and <10% tail latency regression compared to baseline. Unit tests added for scoring logic and CLI dry-run mode.

Usage example: `redwood prefill-handoff scan --range 72h --tenant T123 --out plan.json` produces a plan with recommended batch/cache/quant assignments and an estimated unit-econ delta. `redwood prefill-handoff dry-run --plan plan.json --simulate-traffic=small` runs a local simulator and returns a pass/fail verdict. `redwood prefill-handoff apply --plan plan.json --mode=canary --percent=5` applies recommendations to a small percentage of traffic and watches for fallback signals.

Safety & rollback: the adopter runs with a conservative default policy (allow quant enable only if adoption_score >= 0.75 and simulated token-econ shows >=2% savings). Any observed latency or quality regressions above tenant-configured thresholds trigger a rollback step in the fallback chain. Rollbacks are executed as controller transactions with idempotency keys so they can be retried safely.

Migration notes: to enable this for Dedicated/Private installations operators must run `redwood prefill-handoff init` which registers new telemetry views and an RBAC role (`prefill-adopter`). The CLI can run purely as a planning tool without cluster write privileges.

Testing performed: unit tests, integration tests against a mocked runtime, and a 72-hour smoke simulation on benchmark-lab traces (included as test fixtures). We also ran a canary in staging for two tenants for 48 hours. Observed savings ~3.1% token cost with no detectable quality regression for those tenants.

Rollout plan: merged to main behind a feature flag `prefill_handoff_v1`. Ops will enable the flag for pilot tenants and use the CLI to produce first-run plans. Full rollout will follow after 4 weeks of pilot telemetry review.

Related work: follows the economics/automation direction in ENG-2147 and is intentionally orthogonal to the global batch scheduler changes (this PR only influences tenant-scoped defaults and fallback behavior).

review_comments: Ava Martinez: Please clarify how adoption_score behaves for cold tenants — if there isn't 72h of telemetry do we default to conservative?
Sofia Patel: Response: we default to conservative (score=0.45) and the CLI warns about insufficient data; documented in migration notes.
Ravi Shah: Suggest exposing the fallback chain as a small DSL or JSON schema so operations can compose custom chains. Also request: add a telemetry tag for model_family.
Sofia Patel: Implemented JSON schema for fallback plans and added model_family tag on metrics (see telemetry/econ_metrics.go change).
Clara Nguyen: CI flakes on e2e were caused by a timing assumption in the simulator; pushed a fix to make timeouts deterministic.
Ava Martinez: Approved after minor test naming nits were fixed.
release_notes: Add prefill-handoff CLI for safely adopting tenant-scoped batching/caching/quant defaults. Introduces adoption scoring, fallback chains, and new econ telemetry. Feature gated behind prefill_handoff_v1.
notes_for_ops: Run `redwood prefill-handoff init` after upgrade to register RBAC and telemetry views; use dry-run before apply; feature flag gate is prefill_handoff_v1.
